To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the first nonleading corrections to inclusive hadronic collisions are given by 1/Q2 for unpolarized collisions, and 1/Q for polarized collisions.
the first nonleading corrections in inclusive hadron‐ hadron scattering are of order 1/Q for polarized hadronic scattering, or of order 1/ Q2 for unpolarized hadron‐hadronic collisions.

the first nonleading twist effects in hadron‐hadronic scattering are calculable and that they are of order 1/Q for polarized hadron‐hadrons collisions, or 1/Q2 for unpolarized hadron‐ hadron collisions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following topics: (1) We study inclusive hadron‐ hadron scattering in the high energy limit.
the following questions: 1) How can one describe the nonleading power corrections? 2) How do these corrections arise? 3) How do they depend on the partonic structure of the colliding particles?

the following questions: What are the leading power corrections to inclusive scattering in hadronic collisions? What is the origin of these corrections in terms of the underlying partonic scattering processes? How can these effects be calculated in perturbative quantum chromodynamics?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
high twist effects are not a problem in hadronic scattering.
high twist effects are calculable in perturbative quantum chromodynamics, and that they may be used as a tool to study the structure of the proton and of other hadrons.

the leading power behavior of the cross section is given by a perturbative expansion in powers of 1/Q, and the next‐to‐leading power behavior is given by a nonperturbative expansion in terms of a power series in 1/Q2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the first power corrections in the case of high energy polarized collisions are of the order of 0.01, while in the case of low energy unpolarized collisions they are of the order 0.1.
the nonleading power corrections can be calculated in perturbative quantum chromodynamics, in terms of a few universal distribution functions.
the first nonleading corrections to hadron‐hadronic scattering in perturbative theory are of the order of the square of the momentum transfer, Q2, and the leading twist effects are of the order Q.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, at leading power, inclusive scattering amplitudes in hadronic collisions can be expressed in terms of the same universal parton distribution functions as those that describe deep‐inelastic scattering, and that these parton distribution functions can be measured by deep‐inelastic experiments.
, for the case of polarised hadronic collisions, such corrections are of the same form as the leading twist contribution.
the leading nonperturbative effects in the unpolarized case are due to the transverse momentum of the parton in the initial state.
